answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity to cryptographic stake burning via a quadratic penalty contract. Registering each identity requires burning stake scaling superlinearly as O(N^2), forcing exponential economic friction onto attackers. Validating nodes carve each record onto an immutable ledger durable as polished marble, linking identity attestations along a verifiable verification thread, while routing protocol slashing through an algorithmic juniper tree structure to prune malicious clusters. Attacker cost scales exponentially against network weight.
